div.h3: Medicare Advantage vs. Medicare Supplement: Which Is Right for You?
div.p: Both options help fill gaps in Original Medicare — but they work very differently. This guide walks through the key differences so you can review your options with clarity.

div.h3: Life Insurance Basics for Florida Families

button.span: How much does it cost to work with you?

div.p: Working with Classique Insurance Group is completely free to you. I am compensated by the insurance carrier after enrollment — which means you receive expert guidance, comparison shopping across 27+ carriers, and personalized recommendations at zero cost.

button.span: Who can help me compare Medicare plans in Port Charlotte, Florida?

div.p: Cleveland Bloomfield at Classique Insurance Group can help you compare Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement (Medigap), and Part D plans available in Port Charlotte and throughout Charlotte, Lee, Sarasota, and surrounding counties. Consultations are free and there is no obligation to enroll. Learn more at medicare.gov.

button.span: What states are you licensed in?

div.p: I'm currently licensed in Florida, Texas, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania. While I'm based in Southwest Florida and serve the entire state of Florida, I can help clients in those other states as well. If you're in a different state, reach out — we may still be able to help.

button.span: What's the difference between an independent broker and a captive agent?

div.p: A captive agent works for one company and can only sell that company's products. As an independent broker, I work for you — I have access to 27+ A-rated insurance carriers and can compare plans across all of them to find the one that may truly fit your needs and budget. No bias, no pressure.

button.span: When is the best time to enroll in Medicare?

div.p: The Initial Enrollment Period starts 3 months before your 65th birthday and ends 3 months after. Missing this window can result in late enrollment penalties. The Annual Enrollment Period for plan changes runs October 15 – December 7 each year. I'll help you stay ahead of every deadline. Official guidance is available at medicare.gov.

button.span: What is the difference between Medicare Advantage and Medicare Supplement (Medigap)?

div.p: Medicare Advantage (Part C) replaces Original Medicare through a private plan — often bundling dental, vision, and drug coverage, but with network restrictions. Medicare Supplement (Medigap) works alongside Original Medicare to help cover out-of-pocket costs, often offering broader provider access. The right choice depends on your health, travel habits, and budget. I can walk you through both options at no cost.

button.span: What is an IUL and is it worth reviewing?

div.p: An Indexed Universal Life (IUL) is a permanent life insurance policy that also builds cash value linked to a market index — with a floor designed to limit losses. It may serve as a tax-advantaged retirement income strategy in addition to providing a death benefit. Whether it may be right for you depends on your age, goals, and financial situation. Let's talk — that's what I'm here for.

button.span: What is final expense insurance and do I need it?

div.p: Final expense insurance is a type of whole life policy designed to help cover end-of-life costs such as funeral expenses, medical bills, and outstanding debts. It typically features locked-in premiums and guaranteed or simplified underwriting. It may be worth reviewing if you want to ensure your family is not left with unexpected financial burdens.

button.span: What is life insurance used for and how much coverage might I need?

div.p: Life insurance can help replace lost income, pay off a mortgage, cover final expenses, fund education, or leave a legacy for your family. The right amount of coverage depends on your income, debts, family size, and goals. A free consultation can help you review your options across multiple carriers at no cost to you.

button.span: How does an annuity provide retirement income?

div.p: An annuity is a contract with an insurance company where you contribute a lump sum or payments, and in return may receive a guaranteed income stream — either immediately or at a future date. Annuities can help provide predictable retirement income you may not outlive. Types include fixed, fixed indexed, and income annuities, each with different growth and payout structures.

button.span: Can I get a Marketplace health plan outside of open enrollment?

div.p: Yes, in many cases. If you experience a qualifying life event — such as losing employer coverage, getting married, having a baby, or moving — you may be eligible for a Special Enrollment Period. I'll help you determine your eligibility and review available ACA Marketplace plan options for your family.

button.span: Can Classique Insurance Group help people outside of Port Charlotte?

div.p: Yes. Classique Insurance Group serves clients throughout Southwest Florida — including Punta Gorda, Cape Coral, Fort Myers, North Port, Sarasota, and surrounding communities — as well as the entire state of Florida. I'm also licensed in Texas, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania.

button.span: What happens if I miss my Medicare enrollment window?

div.p: Missing your Initial Enrollment Period may result in a permanent late enrollment penalty added to your premium, and you may need to wait until the General Enrollment Period (January 1 – March 31) to enroll. Some exceptions apply if you have qualifying employer coverage. I can help you understand your situation. More details at ssa.gov/medicare.

button.span: Do I have to pay extra to work with an insurance broker?

div.p: No. Working with an independent insurance broker like Classique Insurance Group costs you nothing extra. Brokers are compensated by the insurance carrier after enrollment. You receive the same or better access to coverage at the same rate — with personalized guidance included at no charge.
